permutationLabel: Severe (Atlanta): persistent respiratory and renal failure >48 h, 40% necrosis, no cholangitis
summary: 64-year-old man on ICU day 3 with gallstone pancreatitis: persistent respiratory failure (SpO₂ 90% on high-flow, RR 30) and renal failure (creatinine 260, oliguria) >48 h, low-dose noradrenaline; CECT: 40% pancreatic necrosis; bilirubin 30, no cholangitis.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Worsening breathing and low urine output on day 3 of admission
inputs.hpi: Admitted 3 days ago with gallstone pancreatitis. Respiratory failure since day 1 (now on high-flow oxygen 60%), oliguric acute kidney injury since day 1, low-dose noradrenaline since this morning. CECT today: 40% pancreatic necrosis with peripancreatic fluid, no gas. No jaundice, bilirubin normal-ish, CBD not dilated.

exam.general: Unwell, tachypnoeic, alert. Temperature 37.9°C, pulse 122/min, BP 92/54 on noradrenaline 0.08 µg/kg/min, RR 30, SpO2 90% on 60% high-flow oxygen.
exam.abdomen: Distended, diffusely tender, no peritonism. Bladder pressure 16 mmHg.
exam.respiratory: Reduced air entry at both bases.

imaging.name: CT abdomen (contrast)
imaging.result: Acute necrotising pancreatitis with approximately 40% parenchymal non-enhancement, extensive peripancreatic fluid, bilateral pleural effusions. No gas. Gallstones; CBD 6 mm.

mustExclude.note: WATERFALL (NEJM 2022) was stopped for harm: aggressive resuscitation (20 mL/kg bolus then 3 mL/kg/h) caused more fluid overload (20.5% vs 6.3%) without benefit. ACG 2024 recommends moderate, goal-directed fluids. A plan that says "aggressive" or 250–500 mL/h is a fluid-overload hazard. In established organ failure with respiratory failure and pleural effusions, fluid overload worsens outcome.
mustExclude.proposedFix: lib/pane-engine management protocol "pancreatitis" (step 1 and the Hartmann's 500 ml Q2H medication), dx-variants.ts pancreatitis_moderate urgencyNote / pancreatitis_severe planPrefix, and clinical-inference.ts pancreatitis prompts: replace "aggressive … 250–500 ml/h" with moderate goal-directed lactated Ringer's (10 mL/kg bolus only if hypovolaemic, then 1.5 mL/kg/h; reassess at 12, 24, 48, 72 h; extra caution in heart failure/CKD/elderly) citing WATERFALL and ACG 2024. Same change in iOS DiagnosisRadiationEngine "acute pancreatitis" planTemplate.

mustExclude.note: Prophylactic antibiotics are not recommended in acute pancreatitis, including predicted severe disease and sterile necrosis; they are reserved for infected necrosis or a concurrent infection such as cholangitis.

ERCP in gallstone pancreatitis only for concurrent cholangitis or persistent biliary obstruction (APEC: no benefit from urgent ERCP without cholangitis). An unconditional ERCP line exposes the patient to post-ERCP pancreatitis and perforation.
Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

dxVariant.proposedFix: dx-variants.ts detectDxVariants: pick the group by diseaseId/ICD across all groups first and use the text fallback only if nothing matched (and make it negation-aware). Today "No cholangitis"/"no pancreatitis" in the assessment selects the earlier Cholangitis/Pancreatitis group by text before the Pancreatitis group is checked by disease id. dx-variants.ts pancreatitis group: test severe → moderately severe → mild with Atlanta phrases that cannot be substrings of each other (e.g. match "moderately severe" before "severe acute pancreatitis"; move "pancreatic necrosis" out of the moderate list or check persistent organ failure first), and accept qualifiers between "mild" and "pancreatitis" (e.g. "mild acute biliary pancreatitis").

guideline.name: Revised Atlanta classification of acute pancreatitis (2012)
guideline.section: Diagnosis (2 of 3: typical pain, lipase/amylase ≥3 × ULN, imaging); severity: mild (no organ failure, no local/systemic complications), moderately severe (transient organ failure <48 h and/or local complications), severe (persistent organ failure >48 h); modified Marshall score
guideline.citation: Banks PA, Bollen TL, Dervenis C, et al. Gut. 2013;62:102–111.

guideline.name: ACG Guideline — management of acute pancreatitis (2024)
guideline.section: Moderately aggressive (goal-directed) fluids with lactated Ringer’s; no prophylactic antibiotics (including predicted severe and sterile necrosis); early oral feeding when tolerated; enteral rather than parenteral nutrition; ERCP within 24 h only with concurrent cholangitis; cholecystectomy during the index admission for mild biliary AP; transabdominal US in every patient; triglycerides if no gallstones/alcohol; CT not needed at presentation unless the diagnosis is unclear
guideline.citation: Tenner S, Vege SS, Sheth SG, et al. Am J Gastroenterol. 2024;119:419–437.

guideline.name: IAP/APA evidence-based guidelines for the management of acute pancreatitis
guideline.section: No antibiotic prophylaxis; enteral nutrition in severe AP; same-admission cholecystectomy for mild biliary AP; delay cholecystectomy with peripancreatic collections until they resolve or beyond 6 weeks; intervention for infected necrosis delayed to ≥4 weeks (walled-off)
guideline.citation: Working Group IAP/APA Acute Pancreatitis Guidelines. Pancreatology. 2013;13(4 Suppl 2):e1–15.

guideline.name: NICE NG104 — Pancreatitis
guideline.section: Acute pancreatitis: do not offer prophylactic antimicrobials; enteral nutrition for moderately severe/severe AP started within 72 h; parenteral nutrition only if enteral nutrition fails or is contraindicated
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NICE guideline NG104, September 2018.

guideline.name: WATERFALL trial — aggressive vs moderate fluid resuscitation in acute pancreatitis (NEJM 2022)
guideline.section: Moderate (10 mL/kg bolus only if hypovolaemic, then 1.5 mL/kg/h lactated Ringer’s) vs aggressive (20 mL/kg bolus then 3 mL/kg/h): stopped for harm — fluid overload 20.5% vs 6.3% with no improvement in moderately severe/severe AP. Patients with heart failure (NYHA II–IV) were excluded
guideline.citation: de-Madaria E, Buxbaum JL, Maisonneuve P, et al. N Engl J Med. 2022;387:989–1000.

guideline.name: APEC trial — urgent ERCP vs conservative treatment in predicted severe gallstone pancreatitis without cholangitis
guideline.section: Urgent ERCP with sphincterotomy did not reduce major complications or mortality in the absence of cholangitis
guideline.citation: Schepers NJ, Hallensleben NDL, Besselink MG, et al. Lancet. 2020;396:167–176.

guideline.name: ESGE guideline — endoscopic management of acute necrotising pancreatitis
guideline.section: No intervention for sterile necrosis; step-up approach for infected necrosis, delayed until walled-off (≈4 weeks)
guideline.citation: Arvanitakis M, Dumonceau JM, Albert J, et al. Endoscopy. 2018;50:524–546.

guideline.name: BISAP score — early prediction of mortality in acute pancreatitis
guideline.section: BUN >25 mg/dL, impaired mental status, SIRS, age >60, pleural effusion within 24 h; ≥3 = increased mortality
guideline.citation: Wu BU, Johannes RS, Sun X, et al. Gut. 2008;57:1698–1703.

guideline.name: AGA Institute guideline on initial management of acute pancreatitis
guideline.section: Goal-directed fluids; against prophylactic antibiotics; against urgent ERCP in biliary AP without cholangitis; early oral feeding (within 24 h); enteral over parenteral; same-admission cholecystectomy for biliary AP; alcohol brief intervention
guideline.citation: Crockett SD, Wani S, Gardner TB, Falck-Ytter Y, Barkun AN. Gastroenterology. 2018;154:1096–1101.

rationale: Permutation: Atlanta severe (persistent organ failure). Requires critical care, avoidance of fluid overload, no prophylactic antibiotics, no ERCP without cholangitis (APEC), enteral nutrition and delayed intervention for necrosis. Also tests that "40% pancreatic necrosis" in the assessment does not demote the dx variant to moderately severe.
